title: Great GASPI Data Schema
perspective: U.S. Federal Government / Financial Oversight and Management Board (FOMB) / Department of the Interior

control_zones.access_restrictions: Subject to federal statutory supremacy under the Territory Clause of the U.S. Constitution.
strategic_features_located_here: Roosevelt Roads Naval Station (former, transferred to local control)

demographics.notes: The population of Puerto Rico in 2024 was 3,198,651. It is a decrease of 0.1% from 2023.

named_high_ground_features.name: El Yunque National Forest
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: Control of observation and movement corridors over the northeastern coastal plain. Position relative to critical watersheds.

named_high_ground_features.name: Cerro de Punta
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: Highest point in the Cordillera Central; control of observation and fire control over interior mountain passes and movement corridors.

physical_barriers.name: Vieques Bombing Range (formerly restricted military zone)
physical_barriers.temporal_variations: Range operations ceased in 2003; cleanup under EPA oversight continues
physical_barriers.stated_justification: Official justification for the US Navy's presence was based on military readiness and national security, citing the strategic importance of the Caribbean. Subsequent federal justification for cleanup has been environmental remediation.
physical_barriers.opposing_characterization: Local communities and environmental groups have characterized the range as a source of environmental contamination and a threat to public health.

water_infrastructure.name: Carraízo Reservoir
water_infrastructure.controlling_entity: PRASA (Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority)

environmental_degradation_incidents.stated_justification: EPA and federal agencies are engaged in remediation efforts under various environmental statutes.
environmental_degradation_incidents.opposing_characterization: Local communities have characterized the area as a health hazard and a failure of environmental enforcement.

airspace_and_spectrum.flight_corridor_control: FAA controlled corridors; SJU airport authority
airspace_and_spectrum.stated_justification: Federal regulation of airspace and telecommunications to ensure safety and uniformity.

maritime_and_cabotage.cabotage_or_merchant_marine_restrictions: The Jones Act (Section 27 of the Merchant Marine Act of 1920) requires that goods shipped between U.S. ports be carried on U.S.-built, U.S.-flagged, and U.S.-crewed vessels.
maritime_and_cabotage.stated_justification: The federal government justifies the Jones Act as a national security measure to maintain a strong U.S. merchant marine and ensure the availability of American-built vessels and mariners for national defense purposes.
maritime_and_cabotage.citation: Merchant Marine Act of 1920; various federal court rulings.

checkpoints_and_gates.name: Port of San Juan (CBP Inspections)
checkpoints_and_gates.permit_type_required: Customs and Border Protection clearance for international cargo and passengers
checkpoints_and_gates.stated_justification: Enforcement of federal immigration, customs, and agricultural laws at the port of entry.

utilities_and_energy_grid.debt_or_fiscal_transfer_mechanisms: The Puerto Rico Oversight, Management, and Economic Stability Act (PROMESA) established the FOMB to oversee fiscal restructuring, including the restructuring of PREPA debt.

jurisprudence_and_statutory_friction.enforced_system_name: Federal statutory supremacy (Title 48 of the U.S. Code, PROMESA, U.S. Constitution)
jurisprudence_and_statutory_friction.preferred_or_prior_system_name: Local Constitution and statutes of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico
enforced_statutes_cited: Article IV, Section 3 of the U.S. Constitution (Territory Clause)
Title 48 of the U.S. Code (Territories and Insular Possessions)
Puerto Rico Oversight, Management, and Economic Stability Act (PROMESA)

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.judicial_body_or_treaty: Supreme Court of the United States
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: Established the doctrine of 'territorial incorporation,' holding that the Constitution does not automatically apply to territories.
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: The U.S. government argued that Puerto Rico was not part of the United States for purposes of the Constitution, justifying the imposition of tariffs on Puerto Rican goods.

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.judicial_body_or_treaty: Supreme Court of the United States
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.case_or_resolution_name: Financial Oversight and Management Board v. Aurelius (140 S. Ct. 1649)
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: Held that members of the FOMB were not 'officers of the United States' under the Appointments Clause.
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: The U.S. government defended the constitutionality of PROMESA and the FOMB's structure.
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.citation: Financial Oversight and Management Board v. Aurelius, 140 S. Ct. 1649 (2020)

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.judicial_body_or_treaty: Supreme Court of the United States
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: Held that Congress can constitutionally exclude Puerto Rico residents from the Supplemental Security Income (SSI) program.
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: The U.S. government argued that treating Puerto Rico differently from states for federal benefits is constitutional under the territorial clauses.

documented_statutory_conflicts.enforced_clause_reference: PROMESA (Board authority to certify fiscal plans and override local laws)
documented_statutory_conflicts.preferred_or_prior_clause_reference: Local Puerto Rico statutes (e.g., Act 22 / Act 60 tax codes)
documented_statutory_conflicts.conflict_description: Conflict between the FOMB's absolute veto power over local fiscal laws and the locally enacted budget and tax laws passed by the Puerto Rican legislature.

official_threat_assessments_or_attack_st.description: Official justifications for fiscal oversight, citing threats to fiscal stability and public safety

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: National security and maintaining a strong U.S. merchant marine.
To provide a mechanism for fiscal stability and debt restructuring in Puerto Rico.
